subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should `claude-cli` long-running background work be supported through a durable OpenClaw host/delivery contract, or should unsupported native Workflow-style affordances be denied consistently?
rationale: Current main has already chosen fail-closed behavior for two native Claude tools, but the remaining Workflow-backed path crosses runtime ownership, plugin/skill exposure, durable session delivery, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Define Durable OpenClaw Longwork
options.body: Keep native unsupported tools denied while designing a supported detached-work path with persisted origin and queued completion delivery.

options.title: Deny All Unsupported Native Longwork
options.body: Treat `claude-cli` as foreground/live-session only and block any native Workflow-style affordance that promises post-turn completion without an OpenClaw delivery route.

options.title: Support Native Claude Background Work
options.body: Invest in a persistent or detached host for Claude-native background jobs and prove completion delivery across turn boundaries before exposing it.

recommendation.title: Define Durable OpenClaw Longwork
recommendation.body: Keep native unsupported tools denied while designing a supported detached-work path with persisted origin and queued completion delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: The warm Claude live-session implementation is the central process-lifetime boundary this decision must extend or constrain.
